title: Come back May 4th to see me react to the winner announcement!! #theat...
transcript: alright theatre nerds, lock in it's my favorite time of year! I know you're wondering “who's in contention to win the coveted Pulitzer Prize for drama” “this year on May 4th?” well you're in luck I'm gonna do a big overview I'm basically gonna run through a wide range of plays from basically least likely to most likely to win building up to my personal top 9 list of contenders first though just to get on the same page we have to talk about some plays that are not eligible starting with anything that has had its world premiere so far in 2026 we're only looking at the calendar year of 2025 we can also rule out any plays that were written by non-American playwrights and we can probably rule out anything that had major New York runs, several years back. then we have some really grey area ones where they very plausibly could be submitted for this year but we just don't know. I would love to see Cold War Choir Practice and Rheology recognized since they both had their premiere in 2025 but they also returned in 2026 so they're allowed to wait if they want and plenty of shows that had regional runs where they could have submitted but we're not sure if they did. Mexodus is a weird one because they had productions in so many different calendar years we have no idea which one they went with but the last grey area one I wanna talk about is Becoming Eve which I think is extremely deserving but it is an adaptation of a memoir and that doesn't disqualify it but it is kind of a demerit. The next grouping of plays that I have up on screen right now are definitely eligible and could very plausibly be in the conversation but for whatever reason either just the vibe or the reception or frankly my personal opinion of the plays I'm not including them in my top nine but now the moment you've been waiting for these are my top nine which is kind of a wishy-washy hybrid of my personal preferences and my predictions starting off with The Great Privation which was this beautiful play about like black mother daughter relationships told in two different centuries next I have Prosperous daughter who's trans in fourth place I have Practice which admittedly is not as obvious of a pick in terms of its subject matter but it's still an exceptional play in my opinion and it examines power have Initiative with a run time of over five hours this is a a quiet epic about coming of age in the early 2000s and a generation inheriting the new woes of the world but in first place a play that classificationReason: Overview of many plays in contention for the Pulitzer Prize for Drama (Cold War Choir Practice, Rheology, Mexodus, and more). No single show is the primary focus; this is a multi-show survey.
